title: diego-santana-inference-reading-log-2026-10
content:
Quick log / scratchpad — things to remember, rough takeaways, and follow-ups from reading around efficient inference (Oct 2026).

Context: running small-medium LLMs for interactive products with tight latency SLOs (<= 150ms p50 for 2k context typical). Mostly looking at attention approximations, KV cache eviction heuristics, adaptive quantization, and practical benchmarking notes. This is not polished, mostly for my own memory and to pass to Owen/Maya for sprint planning.

High-level impressions:
- Paper A (arXiv:2601.01234) on sparse-window attention + shifted global tokens: interesting hybrid that keeps local context fidelity while permitting subquadratic cost. Implementation caveat: kernel selection matters — need fused GPU kernels to avoid tensor memory thrash.
- KV eviction heuristics: naive LRU is simple but bad for long-turn conversational apps where prefix reuse is common. Weighted recency combined with token-type (system vs user) gives better cache hit rate in traces I simulated.
- Quant-aware caching: storing cached KV in a lower-precision layout (int8) works if we keep scaling metadata per block; convert back to float32 only when needed for high-attention-score tokens. Tradeoff: compression speed vs decode overhead.
- MoE routing latency costs are dominated by routing jitter and small-batch gating updates; for dedicated pools, routing can be amortized but for shared-hosted API it's painful. Consider gating fallback to dense smaller model for low-SLA requests.

Notes / snippets from readings:
- On attention approximations: try two modes in runtime config: "local-window+global" for chat and "long-pattern" for chain-of-thought batch jobs. When sequence length <= 1024, full attention. Above that, switch to hybrid.
- Suggested eviction policy prototype: score = alpha*recency_rank + beta*prefix_match + gamma*token_type_bonus. Tune alpha/beta/gamma on sample traces (week-of-traffic).
- Quantization experiment idea: dynamic per-token quant stash. Benchmark path: FP16 model baseline -> static INT8 quant -> adaptive int8-with-block-scale (store scales per 256-token block). Measure latency + perplexity drift on rouge/test prompts.

Concrete experiments to run (short term)
- E1: Implement block-scale INT8 KV store prototype in inference runtime (estimate 4 days). Measure memory reduction and hit conversion cost.
- E2: Run synthetic traces with 'weighted recency' eviction vs LRU for 10k sessions (sample from prod-sim dataset). Metric: token-hit-rate, mean latency, percent of sessions with fallback to model re-encode.
- E3: Microbenchmark hybrid attention kernels on A10 vs H100; see if A10 throughput for local-window is competitive when fused kernels used.

Questions / unknowns to resolve:
- How much psychometric degradation do customers tolerate when we fall back to a smaller model? Need product input (cc: Maya).
- Implementation complexity for storing per-block scales — how heavy on metadata? Could blow up IOPS. Possibly use power-of-two approximate scales to reduce bits.
- Is routing overhead for MoE avoidable with the upcoming compiler optimizations? Need to sync with serving-runtime.

Quick references and bookmarks:
- Implementation notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-eviction-proto (see PR#42) — this PR has a rudimentary weighted-score eviction sim.
- ICLR 2026 workshop slides: "Long-Range Models in Production" (slide pdf saved in shared drive).
- Blog post: "Efficient Attn: hybrid windows" (internal slack link ~#inference-research thread).

Random heuristics I scribbled:
- If session average turn length < 64 tokens, prioritize recency over prefix-match (alpha >> beta).
- For sessions with > 5 system messages, boost system tokens to never evict (delta flag).
- When cache hit rate drops below 60% on a user cohort, flip to aggressive summarization + reindexing to save memory.

Follow-ups (assignments):
- Diego: prototype per-block scale KV (due: Oct 29) — will drop a PR with microbenchmarks.
- Maya: check product tolerances for model-fallback TTL and generate guidance.
- Owen: coordinate with serving-runtime on fused kernel availability for A10.

Meeting notes bits (from sync 2026-10-26):
- Team agreed to pilot E1 on one dedicated pool.
- SRE concerned about metadata write amplification; propose batching metadata writes with a low-latency write coalescer.
- Product wants a one-pager showing cost savings vs quality drop for three different policies: LRU baseline, weighted eviction, and summarization-on-evict.

Little experiments / logs (ad-hoc):
- Local run: sample trace of 100 sessions with weighted eviction (alpha=0.6,beta=0.3,gamma=0.1) -> hit rate 71% vs LRU 62%. Latency p95 increased by +8ms (due to scale-conversion).
- Small batch quant test: block-scale int8 reduced KV mem by ~3.8x, encode/decode overhead +6ms per token on A10. Need to test H100 which may have lower conversion overhead.

To read / next in queue:
- "Adapter fusion for inference" (paper pdf) — interested in how to fuse adapters at runtime for multi-tenant model variants.
- "MoE routing at scale" — focus on routing stability and cold-start penalty.
- Practical guide: "Quantization gotchas" — blog, has checklist for LSD (latency-sensitive deployment).

Triage / quick TODOs (one-line):
- [ ] Draft one-pager for product: cost vs quality for 3 eviction policies (Maya + Diego).
- [ ] Start E1 prototype branch and bench with A10 (Diego).
- [ ] Schedule sync w/ serving-runtime about fused kernels (Owen).

End of scratchpad. Keep iterating — will convert to formal tech note after experiments.
